Implementation and tests for Story docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md are present and passing.
1) Rule implementation - File: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts - Adds configurable options for patterns and examples: - interface AnnotationRuleOptions { story?: { pattern?: string; example?: string }; req?: { pattern?: string; example?: string }; storyPathPattern?: string; storyPathExample?: string; requirementIdPattern?: string; requirementIdExample?: string; } - Provides defaults: - getDefaultStoryPattern(): /^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$/ - getDefaultStoryExample(): "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md" - getDefaultReqPattern(): /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/ - getDefaultReqExample(): "REQ-EXAMPLE" - resolvePattern(...) chooses nested > flat > default and validates regex via new RegExp(...), pushing error messages into optionErrors on failure: - buildInvalidRegexError(field, pattern) -> `Invalid regular expression for option "${field}": "${pattern}"` - On invalid regex, resolvePattern returns the provided defaultPattern (backward compatibility fallback). - resolveExample(...) chooses nested example > flat example > default example, ensuring custom examples appear in error messages. - resolveOptions(rawOptions) normalizes options, uses resolvePattern / resolveExample to produce ResolvedAnnotationOptions { storyPattern: RegExp; storyExample: string; reqPattern: RegExp; reqExample: string }, updates a global resolvedDefaults, and resets/populates optionErrors. - getRuleSchema() returns a proper JSON Schema array for ESLint rule meta: - properties: story (object with pattern/example), req (object with pattern/example), storyPathPattern, storyPathExample, requirementIdPattern, requirementIdExample - additionalProperties: false - JSDoc explicitly ties this helper to Story 010.1 and its requirements: - @story docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md - @req REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG, REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES, REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION
- File: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts - buildStoryErrorMessage(kind, value, options) uses options.storyExample (with fallback STORY_EXAMPLE_PATH) to embed the configured story example in error messages: - Missing: `Missing story path for @story annotation. Expected a path like "${example}".` - Invalid: `Invalid story path "${value}" for @story annotation. Expected a path like "${example}".` - buildReqErrorMessage(kind, value, options) uses options.reqExample (with fallback getDefaultReqExample()) to embed the configured requirement example in error messages: - Missing: `Missing requirement ID for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like "${example}".` - Invalid: `Invalid requirement ID "${value}" for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like "${example}" (uppercase letters, numbers, and dashes only).` - This satisfies REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES by wiring examples into message construction.
- File: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - Imports and uses the new helpers: - import { getResolvedDefaults, resolveOptions, type ResolvedAnnotationOptions, getRuleSchema, getOptionErrors } from "./helpers/valid-annotation-options"; - meta.schema is set to getRuleSchema(), directly using the JSON Schema from the helper (REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION, Quality Standards AC). - meta.messages includes a configuration error message tied to 010.1: - invalidRuleConfiguration: "Invalid configuration for valid-annotation-format: {{details}}" - JSDoc: @story docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md, @req REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION, REQ-BACKWARD-COMP - create(context): - const options = resolveOptions(context.options || []); // builds ResolvedAnnotationOptions using defaults or configured patterns - const optionErrors = getOptionErrors(); - Program(node): if optionErrors.length > 0, reports each with messageId "invalidRuleConfiguration" and the precise detail string from buildInvalidRegexError. - Then iterates all comments and calls processComment(context, comment, options), meaning that even with invalid regex config, the rule continues using default patterns (REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT). - JSDoc for create and Program explicitly reference Story 010.1 and requirements REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION and REQ-BACKWARD-COMP, showing intent to satisfy this story.
2) Rule documentation - File: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md - Explicitly documents that patterns are configurable and describes both nested and flat shorthand options: - Nested: - story.pattern / story.example - req.pattern / req.example - Flat shorthand: - storyPathPattern - storyPathExample - requirementIdPattern - requirementIdExample - Explains precedence: when both nested and flat are provided for the same value, nested configuration takes precedence (aligns with resolvePattern/resolveExample behavior). - Provides clear configuration examples that match the story's acceptance criteria and examples: - Nested custom configuration example using story.pattern and req.pattern. - Flat shorthand configuration example with storyPathPattern/storyPathExample and requirementIdPattern/requirementIdExample. - Describes invalid configuration behavior: - If any pattern field contains an invalid regex source, the rule reports an ESLint configuration diagnostic with messageId "invalidRuleConfiguration" and falls back to built-in defaults for actual validation. - This documentation directly addresses the "Documentation" acceptance criterion and REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG / REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION / REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES.

Test: "[REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG] nested req.pattern takes precedence over flat requirementIdPattern and its example" similarly validates precedence for req.
